channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Comedian Broda Shaggi recounts stray bullet injury
item.description: Nollywood actor Samuel Perry, known as Broda Shaggi, described his fear and uncertainty after being shot by a stray bullet while filming a skit.

item.title: Nigeria places 46 Ebola contacts on no-fly list
item.description: Authorities have imposed a 21-day travel restriction on individuals who had contact with an Ebola-infected person as part of containment efforts.

item.title: Sierra Leone regulator's revenue rises to NLE 7.4 million
item.description: The Sierra Leone Electricity and Water Regulatory Commission (SLEWRC) saw internal revenue climb from NLE 2.3 million in 2023 to NLE 7.4 million in 2024.

item.title: African youths question growth amid unrest
item.description: Protests erupted across the continent demanding better governance and economic relief as elections fueled anger and conflicts escalated.

item.title: Female artisanal miners in Kono report systemic sexual violence
item.description: Women working in diamond and gold pits in Sierra Leone face persistent threats of rape and harassment while struggling to earn a daily livelihood.

item.title: Sierra Leone vice presidents lack presidential succession path
item.description: The office, constitutionally powerful, has historically served as a political cul-de-sac rather than a stepping stone to the presidency.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation and health risks
item.description: The widespread use of charcoal for cooking, driven by limited access to electricity and gas, is leading to significant deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions in Sierra Leone.

item.title: Mauritius police search for uncle after child sexual abuse video surfaces
item.description: Authorities are seeking a 27-year-old man after a video on social media showed the sexual abuse of a six-year-old girl in Mauritius.

item.title: Labour Congress seeks risk allowance for more workers
item.description: The Mauritius Labour Congress is demanding that the risk allowance granted to police officers be extended to other essential service providers.

item.title: Journalist sidelined amid French media ban talks
item.description: France 24's correspondent in Togo and Benin was suddenly removed from her post in September, as France seeks to restore broadcast access.

item.title: Tunis police arrest three brothers for drug trafficking
item.description: Authorities seized cocaine, a scale, and cash during a raid on a home in El Hafsia, Tunis.

item.title: Liberian senator questions education ministry's centralized system
item.description: Senator Prince Kermue Moye argues the Ministry of Education's central control weakens county officials' authority over teachers and payroll.

item.title: Copper Princesses lose to Venezuela on late goal
item.description: Zambia's U-17 Women's National Team conceded a dramatic winner in stoppage time, falling 2-1 to Venezuela in the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup.

item.title: Saido Berahino retires from English football to coach Burundi
item.description: The former West Bromwich Albion striker returns to his birth nation to train the national team, the Intamba Mu Rugamba.

item.title: Standard Chartered names Adelagun CEO
item.description: Ayodeji Adelagun has been confirmed as the new Chief Executive Officer of Standard Chartered Bank Nigeria Limited after serving as acting CEO since January.

item.title: Paris loses to Barcelona in four-goal thriller
item.description: Two early injuries to key players did not deter Paris from a spirited comeback, ultimately falling short in a high-scoring match.

item.title: Benin lawmakers to review new road traffic code
item.description: Parliamentarians will consider proposed measures including legal alcohol limits and child restraint systems during the current session.

item.title: Civil society leaders on hunger strike in gendarmerie
item.description: Five Central African Republic civil society leaders are on a hunger strike in gendarmerie custody after being denied food and water by police.

item.title: Chad youth face bleak future due to poor health and education
item.description: Young Chadians are seen as a burden, with public services in health and education increasingly outsourced to the private sector.

item.title: Liberian education minister to lead delegation to Canada
item.description: Liberia's education minister will head a delegation to Toronto to discuss partnerships and investment in the country's education sector.

item.title: Sudan talks resume in Geneva amid deepening crisis
item.description: Representatives from 21 countries and five international institutions met to discuss ceasefires, security, and political solutions to the ongoing conflict.

item.title: IMF mission reviews Ghana's 2027 budget plans
item.description: Discussions will focus on fiscal performance, revenue, inflation, and debt as Ghana seeks to consolidate economic gains.

item.title: Ghana targets AI facility within 24 months
item.description: The government aims to complete the first phase of a national computing facility to boost local artificial intelligence development.

item.title: Liberian journalists secure 140 India training slots
item.description: The Female Journalists Association of Liberia has secured 140 training opportunities in India for women journalists, focusing on digital media and leadership.

item.title: Ghana's National Investment Bank returns to profit
item.description: The bank's capital adequacy ratio rose to 23% after a government cash injection and bond offering.

item.title: Kolwezi protests leave two injured and property damaged
item.description: Artisanal miners demonstrated for two days in Kolwezi, paralyzing economic activity and causing injuries and material damage.

item.title: Minister tells off parliament speaker over corruption claims
item.description: Information Minister Shadric Namalomba has demanded evidence from Parliament Speaker Sameer Suleman regarding alleged corruption within the government.

item.title: Namibia orders audits into traditional fishing funds
item.description: Minister James Sankwasa announced planned audits into traditional authorities' fishing quota funds due to unexplained withdrawals.

item.title: Benin finance minister forecasts 300 billion CFA franc surplus
item.description: The minister of finance announced the projected surplus for public companies and offices in 2025 at a Cotonou accounting congress.

item.title: DR Congo official banned from media over threats
item.description: Fils Mukoko, an official of the ruling UDPS party, faces media ban and judicial inquiry for inciting violence against Western nationals.

item.title: Parliament interviews candidates for judiciary watchdog
item.description: Six shortlisted individuals are being vetted by lawmakers to fill positions on a new commission intended to oversee judicial conduct.

item.title: Analyst urges Ghana to boost farm extension services
item.description: Dr Joseph Opoku Gakpo says stronger support for agricultural extension personnel is essential to improving food security and farmer innovation.

item.title: Ligue Pro du Bénin names media commission
item.description: The Benin Professional Football League has appointed a new ad hoc media commission to improve relations with clubs and journalists.

item.title: Ratovomanana Jaovolahasy receives arts and culture award
item.description: The founder and leader of the gospel band Jaws Band was honored for his contributions to Malagasy arts.

item.title: Scouts launch new academic year
item.description: Madagascar's Scouts opened the 2026-2027 academic year with an official ceremony and the distribution of neckerchiefs.

item.title: Rotary and WHO organize march against polio
item.description: A public march will take place in Antananarivo on October 24, 2026, to raise awareness and combat polio.

item.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola Bundibugyo strain
item.description: The World Health Organisation stated that the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, confirmed in Nigeria's capital, has no vaccine or specific treatment.

item.title: Viyuyi and Kondowe share top scorer lead
item.description: Standard Bank Blue Eagles striker Tonic Viyuyi has drawn level with FCB Nyasa Bullets striker Ephraim Kondowe on 10 goals each in the FDH Bank Premiership.

item.title: Namibia government to cap private student funding
item.description: Education minister Sanet Steenkamp told parliament that parents must cover tuition shortfalls for private tertiary students.

item.title: Namibia finance minister to review N$8.5bn development spending
item.description: The finance minister will present the 2026/2027 Mid-Year Budget Review, detailing spending, revenue collection, and government liquidity.

item.title: Mali traffic alternates on RN27 from October 19
item.description: The Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure has reintroduced alternating traffic on a section of Bamako's Route Nationale 27 to allow for roadworks.

item.title: Rotary clubs march against polio
item.description: Community groups in Antananarivo will hold a four-kilometer walk to raise awareness for polio eradication efforts.

item.title: Pupil accuses teacher of sexual assault at high school
item.description: Four teachers at Sikhunyane High School are suspended amid allegations of inappropriate relationships with students, including a sexual assault claim.

item.title: OK Foods boss offers space to young entrepreneurs
item.description: Lincoln Motsa has opened his new commercial premises to three young entrepreneurs, creating 29 jobs in total.

item.title: Mauritius poverty rate to fall below 10% by 2028
item.description: Projections show a sustained decrease in poverty, despite imported inflation and currency depreciation impacting purchasing power.

item.title: Burkina Faso and Turkey discuss defense pact
item.description: Officials from both nations met in Ankara to explore enhanced cooperation in security, health, and economic sectors.

item.title: Poura CEB teacher receives motorcycle for perfect exam results
item.description: Bouma Nebié was awarded a motorcycle and cash for achieving a 100% pass rate for his 59 students in the 2026 CEP exams.

item.title: Austrian and Swiss hostages freed in Libya
item.description: Eva Gretzmacher and Claudia Abbt, kidnapped in Niger in 2025, arrived in Benghazi after more than a year in captivity.

item.title: Camara elected Ivory Coast Senate president
item.description: Kandia Kamissoko Camara, a former English teacher and minister, has been elected president of the Ivorian Senate.

item.title: Ivory Coast completes 220 child labor actions
item.description: A joint initiative by Solidaridad West Africa and Olam Food Ingredients has reported an 88% execution rate on planned actions against child labor.

item.title: Morocco divorce cases rise 4.38% in 2025
item.description: Total divorce and judicial separation filings reached 154,377, reversing a slight decline from the previous year, according to judicial data.

item.title: Tunis court postpones journalist Zied El-Heni trial
item.description: The journalist's support committee is demanding his release after the case, which concerns leaked recordings, was adjourned for the fifth time.

item.title: DER/FJ disburses 65.5 million CFA to 27 groups in Matam
item.description: The General Delegation for Rapid Entrepreneurship for Women and Youth has provided funding to 675 beneficiaries in Matam, urging greater youth involvement in business.

item.title: Morocco beat Angola 5-2 to win fourth Futsal AFCON title
item.description: The Atlas Lions secured their fourth consecutive continental championship by defeating Angola in the final on home soil.

item.title: Senegal unions report low strike turnout in Tivaouane
item.description: Only 29% of education staff and 21% of health workers joined a 72-hour strike in Tivaouane, according to official figures.

item.title: Mabandla denies halting TRC prosecutions
item.description: Former justice minister Brigitte Mabandla told the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry she did not instruct a moratorium on post-TRC cases.

item.title: Boy, 11, found dead as Ziz river levels rise
item.description: Rescue teams recovered the body of an 11-year-old boy swept away by the swollen Ziz River in Erfoud, Morocco, following heavy rainfall.

item.title: African Union Commission president reaffirms human rights commitment
item.description: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf pledged continued dedication to dignity, justice, and equality on the 40th anniversary of the African Charter.

item.title: Senegalese artist reaffirms Niger development support
item.description: Singer Coumba Gawlo Seck met President Tiani to pledge her commitment to Niger's growth and cultural promotion.

item.title: Angola president promises end to hunger by 2027
item.description: President João Lourenço claims the ruling MPLA party will reveal a method for Angolans to live without eating by the next general election.

item.title: Le Soleil newspaper discusses archives with Dakar archbishop
item.description: The national daily's director general met with Archbishop André Guèye to explore covering Catholic events and using church records.

item.title: African Development Bank donates equipment to Guinea-Bissau government
item.description: The donation aims to modernize public administration and improve service delivery to citizens.

item.title: Mozambique discusses cannabis legalisation
item.description: A national drugs conference in Maputo considered the commercial possibilities of cannabis, acknowledging its medicinal and economic potential.

item.title: Teachers union demands overdue payments and reclassifications
item.description: Guinea-Bissau's national teachers union warns of class disruptions if overdue payments and reclassifications for 1,112 educators are not addressed.

item.title: Africa Eco Race to cross Morocco's southern provinces in January
item.description: The 18th edition of the rally will start in Tangier and pass through Laayoune and Dakhla before entering Mauritania, following past disruptions.

item.title: Cotonou closes city hall access for road work
item.description: Road construction on streets 12 007 and 12 048 will block access to Cotonou's city hall for three months starting October 26.

item.title: Nigerien military schools compete in first tournament
item.description: 12 delegations from Niger's defense and security training institutions are participating in a 10-day sports competition in Zinder.

item.title: South Sudan condemns deadly market bombing in Abyei
item.description: Juba demands an investigation and emergency humanitarian access after an October 19 airstrike on Amiet market caused civilian casualties and damage.

item.title: Niger communication chief visits Algerian news agency
item.description: Niger's National Communication Observatory president met with APS officials to strengthen information and communication ties.

item.title: Algeria coach considers positional changes amid defensive shortages
item.description: Coach Ibrahim Hamdani is exploring shifting players to new roles to address a lack of central defenders before upcoming matches.

item.title: Guinea launches public finance reform plan
item.description: The government has launched a strategic plan to reform public finances from 2026 to 2030, aiming for systemic transformation.

item.title: Algerian MPs limited to two questions monthly
item.description: The National People's Assembly has set a limit of two oral questions per deputy per month to streamline parliamentary oversight.

item.title: Kiir removes longtime minister Lomuro from cabinet
item.description: President Salva Kiir has replaced Martin Elia Lomuro, who served for nearly two decades, with Bol Wek Agoth as minister of cabinet affairs.

item.title: Kankan court convicts five for shisha, 28 face cannabis charges
item.description: Judicial proceedings in Kankan have resulted in prison sentences and fines for shisha use, with a separate group awaiting trial for cannabis offenses.

item.title: Media wins sight of SSA secrecy application in R12 million fraud trial
item.description: News organisations have obtained a redacted copy of the State Security Agency’s application to close the corruption trial of two former senior officials.

item.title: Morocco's Mansouri defends new government structure
item.description: The head of government addressed parliament, explaining decisions on ministerial appointments and budget deadlines.

item.title: Malian fashion show highlights traditional clothing
item.description: The sixth Koko Fashion Show in Bamako will showcase traditional Malian attire and craftsmanship.

item.title: Libya signs food security deal with Islamic organization
item.description: The agriculture minister and the Islamic Organization for Food Security agreed to a framework for cooperation on livestock and crop production.

item.title: Lawmaker announces no-confidence vote against agriculture minister
item.description: A national lawmaker plans to introduce a motion of no-confidence against the Minister of State for Agriculture and Food Security over alleged embezzlement of $57 million.

item.title: Egypt president says military action to defend Saudi Arabia
item.description: President Al-Sisi stated Egypt's proposed military effort is solely for defending Saudi territory and not for attacking Yemen.

item.title: Boké officials injured in mining road crash
item.description: The governorate's cabinet director and regional mines inspector were seriously hurt when their vehicle collided with a mining truck.

item.title: Chinsali council seeks business input for 2027 budget
item.description: Local authorities met with traders to align proposed development projects with district priorities for the upcoming fiscal year.

item.title: Kaputa health director urges cholera vigilance
item.description: Jonathan Bwalya calls for public cooperation in preventing the spread of the waterborne disease.

item.title: Mauritania approves decree for local drug manufacturing
item.description: A new government decree aims to regulate pharmaceutical factories, boost domestic supply, and reduce reliance on imported medicines.

item.title: Mauritania adopts 2027 budget with 152 billion ouguiya revenue
item.description: The government's finance bill projects a 6.2 billion ouguiya surplus and 0.5% economic growth amid global economic risks.

item.title: Japan explores Angola cooperation strategies
item.description: Japanese business delegation and Angolan minister discuss maritime transport, logistics, and financial services to boost national production.

item.title: Chad launches project to boost legume and fodder crop value chains
item.description: The TARSPro II project aims to empower women economically and improve food security in Mayo-Kebbi Ouest province.

item.title: Godongwana cuts fuel levy to offer relief
item.description: Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana announced a reduction in the fuel levy to provide temporary relief to South Africans from November 4.

item.title: Mauritanian official reassigned after power station fires
item.description: Akhrambali Ould Mohamed Lehbib moves to hydrocarbons company one week after dismissal from electricity firm following an investigation into recent fires.

item.title: Military personnel tortured and jailed amid leak accusations
item.description: 201 soldiers face detention and mistreatment in Black Beach prison following allegations of leaking sensitive information.

item.title: KFC launches Kenyan-inspired food and entertainment campaign
item.description: The fast-food chain introduces a limited-time menu and retail activations with local creatives in Nairobi.

item.title: Bard Santner appoints international board for diaspora banking
item.description: The microfinance bank has appointed a 13-member board with former executives from major financial institutions to oversee its strategy.

item.title: Faye links Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics to Africa's global standing
item.description: Senegal's president sees the games as a chance to boost the continent's visibility and argue for a permanent UN Security Council seat.

item.title: Kenya plans tougher laws against illicit alcohol cartels
item.description: The government will introduce stricter legislation and boost enforcement to dismantle criminal networks involved in the production and sale of harmful alcoholic drinks.

item.title: Eswatini calls for regional action on supply chain woes
item.description: The kingdom's foreign minister urged stronger cooperation to counter rising costs and trade disruptions affecting COMESA nations.

item.title: Algerian social security agency adopts electronic signatures
item.description: The CNAS is preparing to integrate digital certification into its administrative processes to modernize operations and reduce paperwork.

item.title: Eswatini stars close in on Zimbabwe league title
item.description: Hardrock FC, featuring five Eswatini internationals, needs three wins to secure the Castle Lager Premier Soccer League championship.

item.title: Mozambique faces questions over millions of children out of school
item.description: Millions of children are not in school in Mozambique, raising concerns about the quality of education and future competencies.

item.title: Cameroon seeks UK finance for timber processing
item.description: Yaoundé wants British support to modernize its timber industry, focusing on small businesses and technology upgrades.

item.title: Hungley urges African Charter use amid rising costs
item.description: Mauritius's Vice-President Robert Hungley called for greater reliance on the African Charter for Human Rights to address current population challenges.
